MELON price collapses roughly 10x further under expansion_oriented than under the inert

market_effects.finding: protagonist revenue is dramatically lower (~69% reduction) facing expansion_oriented and
aggressive_investment than any other archetype. Direct market-price telemetry confirms
MELON's price crashes far harder when facing expansion_oriented than the passive control,
consistent with a shared-market oversupply mechanism from the opponent's own heavy
MELON production/selling -- this is EXPERIMENTALLY SUPPORTED by observed price data,
though a fully isolated causal intervention (varying only the opponent's selling volume,
holding everything else fixed) was not run this phase.

economic_effects.expansion_oriented: catastrophic for the protagonist -- 0% win rate, ~85% revenue reduction
economic_effects.aggressive_investment: significant for the protagonist -- 40% loss rate, ~46% revenue reduction
economic_effects.all_others: no measurable negative economic effect on the protagonist relative to the passive control

features_rejected: no feature was found USELESS outright at the tested checkpoints -- money-based and land/hire-event
features dominated top-feature-importance rankings; tile-diversity (entropy/concentration) features
unsupervised clustering (no labels) achieved only 57-71% alignment vs. the supervised classifier's
85-95% -- clustering alone is NOT recommended as a production detector, only as a discovery-phase
sanity check that real structure exists without label leakage

limitations: Market-effect analysis is correlational only -- no causal intervention experiment (e.g. holding an
archetype's production fixed while varying only its market activity) was run this phase.
Only 7 pre-existing Phase 3.1 archetypes were tested -- no new archetype was invented, per the
brief's instruction, so regimes outside this set (e.g. a genuinely mixed/adaptive real opponent)
The NearestCentroidClassifier and simple_kmeans are both deliberately simple (no sklearn/neural
methods) -- a more sophisticated model was never attempted since the simple one already showed
strong separation (per the brief's explicit instruction not to overengineer).
Held-out n=6 seeds per archetype (42 held-out episodes total) is modest; the 15/15 expansion_oriented
loss finding is robust ACROSS all three seed sets combined (45 total episodes, 0 protagonist wins),
which is the stronger claim actually being made.
The root economic MECHANISM behind the expansion_oriented vulnerability was not diagnosed at the
transaction level this phase (e.g. confirming via market price telemetry that crop prices crashed)
-- flagged as the top candidate follow-up, not yet confirmed.
